cards.definition: To cook food using dry heat in an oven.
To cook food over direct heat, usually on a grill.
To spoon or brush liquid or fat over food while it cooks to keep it moist.
To mix ingredients rapidly to incorporate air and create a smooth texture.
To briefly cook food in boiling water, then cool it quickly in ice water.
To combine ingredients until smooth and evenly mixed.
To cook food in liquid at 100°C until bubbles continuously rise to the surface.
To remove bones from meat, poultry, or fish.
To slowly cook food in a small amount of liquid after browning it.
To coat food with flour, egg, and breadcrumbs before cooking.
To cook food using intense heat from above or below.
To cook food until its surface develops a golden-brown colour.
To heat sugar until it melts and turns golden brown, or to slowly brown vegetables to develop sweetness.
To cut food into roughly even-sized pieces.
To make a liquid clear by removing impurities, or to separate butterfat from milk solids.
To evenly cover food with a sauce, flour, crumbs, or other ingredient.
To mix two or more ingredients together.
To remove the center of fruits such as apples or pears.
To beat butter and sugar together until light and fluffy.
To cut food into evenly sized square pieces.
To add liquid to a hot pan to dissolve browned food particles for a sauce.
To cut food into small, even cubes.
To remove excess liquid from food.
To lightly sprinkle food with flour, icing sugar, or another dry ingredient.
To remove bones from fish or slice meat into boneless portions.
To gently combine ingredients while keeping as much air as possible in the mixture.
To cook food in hot oil or fat.
To decorate food to improve its appearance and sometimes add flavor.
To coat food with a shiny finish using egg wash, syrup, or sauce.
To shred food into fine pieces using a grater.
To coat a pan or tray with fat to prevent sticking.
To cut food into thin, matchstick-sized strips.
To work dough by pressing, folding, and stretching to develop gluten.
To soak food in a seasoned liquid to add flavor and tenderness.
To crush cooked food into a smooth or coarse consistency.
To accurately determine the amount of an ingredient using scales or measuring tools.
To cut food into very small pieces or grind it finely.
To combine ingredients until evenly distributed.
To remove the outer skin of fruits or vegetables.
To gently cook food in liquid below boiling point (approximately 70–85°C).
To bring an oven or cooking equipment to the required temperature before use.
To blend food until completely smooth.
To simmer a liquid until it thickens.
To cook food using dry heat in an oven, often uncovered.
To cook food quickly in a small amount of fat over high heat.
To make shallow cuts on the surface of food to assist cooking or presentation.
To cook the outside of food quickly over high heat to develop color and flavor.
To add salt, pepper, herbs, spices, or other flavorings to food.
To cut or tear food into long, thin strips.
To pass dry ingredients through a sieve to remove lumps and add air.
To cook food gently in liquid just below boiling point (approximately 85–95°C).
To cut food into thin, even pieces.
To cook food using steam from boiling water without the food touching the water.
To cook food slowly in liquid over low heat.
To move ingredients around with a spoon or spatula to combine or prevent sticking.
To make meat softer by mechanical or chemical methods.
To brown food using dry heat.
To gently mix ingredients, often salads, without crushing them.
To remove unwanted fat, skin, or damaged portions from food.
To beat ingredients rapidly to incorporate air and increase volume.
To beat ingredients using a whisk to blend or add air.
To remove the coloured outer skin of citrus fruit without the bitter white pith.
